display_name: Sweep the fleet for a stall, keyed on produced work
description: Returns data {job_id, status: queued} after persisting the request. Read service_interface::job_service::get_job with that exact job_id; schedule another read while queued or processing. Only a terminal successful job provides the original complete response in job.result (the original data is job.result.data); failures preserve the original response in job.result and the error in job.error. Do not repeat the operation because its completion has not been read. iss_ebc1ce9c and iss_c4fbe548. Detects a stalled fleet by what it has PRODUCED, for any agent runtime. Over a window (window_seconds, default 1800) it reads two register facts through the existing read-only psolet CLI port: the Units whose coverage is 'active-owned' (live, owned and unexpired work someone is supposed to be moving), and, for each distinct actor that owns one, that actor's register-recorded produced artifacts since the window opened (Unit state events, read-backs, candidate revisions, landings, issue events). The verdict is 'stalled' when work was ready and owned and those actors produced nothing in the window, 'not_stalled' when something was produced OR nothing was ready and owned (an idle fleet with no work is not a stall), and 'unmeasured' when a read did not complete. Sessions are enumerated runtime-neutrally from the managed_session ledger through StateManagementInterface and carried into the report with their agent_runtime and lifecycle_state, so a Codex-only fleet is covered identically to a Claude one; the verdict never depends on which runtime is present, on a session count, on ~/.claude/sessions or on any liveness signal. This is the gap seat_idle_watcher cannot cover: that watcher is Claude-only and single-seat by construction and keys on a status file saying 'idle'. REPORT ONLY: this verb never drives, clears, compacts, terminates or spawns a session, and the module imports nothing that could. It refuses nothing; an incomplete read yields a named advisory and NO verdict rather than a manufactured stall from an unreadable register. Every completed run, advisory runs included, publishes itself so read_fleet_stall_sweep_status can tell when the sweep has stopped running.
embedding_description: Checking whether the whole agent fleet has stalled by comparing what it actually produced in the register over the last half hour against the work that is ready and owned, covering Codex and Claude sessions alike, and reporting a stalled, not-stalled or unmeasured verdict without touching any session.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: job_id and status=queued. Retrieve the exact job; the former final response is in job.result. verdict (stalled | not_stalled | unmeasured), trigger, completed_at, window_seconds, window_since, ready_and_owned_count, produced_count, owning_actors, session_count, runtime_counts, advisories, and the full ready_and_owned, produced and sessions rows the verdict was computed from.
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: A queued receipt confirms acceptance only. Retrieve the terminal job before presenting any outcome. Lead with the verdict and the two counts it came from: how much work was ready and owned, and how much was produced in the window. Name the window explicitly, because 'nothing produced' means nothing inside that window and nothing else. State runtime_counts so a reader can see the fleet is being measured across runtimes rather than for Claude alone. Treat verdict='unmeasured' as exactly that: read the advisories aloud and do NOT describe the fleet as healthy or as stalled, because no verdict was computed. Never present session_count or an idle-looking session as evidence of a stall; this signal is output, not liveness.
result_processor_customizations.output_action_guidance: A stalled verdict is a report for a seat to act on, not an instruction this verb carries out: nothing here wakes, clears or spawns anything, by design. read_fleet_stall_sweep_status shows whether the sweep itself is still running. ensure_fleet_stall_sweep_schedule installs its cron if a deployment has none.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: One StateManagementInterface read of the managed_session ledger and one or more read-only psolet CLI invocations (db unit who-has-work, db activity produced-work), followed by a single key_value_store write publishing this run. No session is contacted and no register row is written.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: parameter_invalid: window_seconds was not a positive integer. state_service_unavailable: the deployment has no bound state service, so neither the ledger nor the run record is reachable. A register CLI refusal or an incomplete ledger read is NOT an error here: it is returned as a named advisory with verdict='unmeasured'.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: Retry is always safe; every read is read-only and the run record is a single overwritten latest-run row. For verdict='unmeasured', read the advisory: it names which read did not complete and why, usually an unreachable or misconfigured psolet CLI (the psolet_cli config key) or a ledger page that exceeded its bounded-read ceiling. Fix the named read rather than treating the absent verdict as calm.
